variants.title: Hall effect in n-type germanium
variants.sample: n-type germanium crystal (carrier number set by its doping, not a material constant)
variants.unknown: the Hall coefficient, carrier type and carrier number of an n-type crystal
variants.note: The Hall voltage comes out negative: the carriers are electrons. The carrier number belongs to this particular doped crystal; what IS a property of germanium is the electron mobility, about 0.39 m2/Vs at 300 K, which the Hall coefficient and the resistivity together give back.

source.title: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics / S. M. Sze, Physics of Semiconductor Devices: germanium electron mobility 0.39 m2/Vs and hole mobility 0.19 m2/Vs at 300 K

variants.title: Hall effect in p-type germanium
variants.sample: p-type germanium crystal (carrier number set by its doping, not a material constant)
variants.unknown: the Hall coefficient, carrier type and carrier number of a p-type crystal
variants.note: The same apparatus, the same field, the same current - and the Hall voltage comes out with the opposite sign. That sign is the whole point: the carriers here are holes. The resistivity and the Hall coefficient together give a mobility near germanium's hole value of 0.19 m2/Vs.

source.title: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics / S. M. Sze, Physics of Semiconductor Devices: germanium electron mobility 0.39 m2/Vs and hole mobility 0.19 m2/Vs at 300 K

variants.title: Hall effect in lightly doped germanium
variants.sample: Lightly doped n-type germanium (carrier number set by its doping, not a material constant)
variants.unknown: the Hall coefficient and carrier number of a lightly doped crystal
variants.note: Ten times fewer carriers, so ten times the Hall voltage for the same current and field: the Hall coefficient is 1/(ne), which is why the effect is used to measure carrier numbers and why metals, packed with electrons, show almost no Hall voltage at all.

source.title: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics / S. M. Sze, Physics of Semiconductor Devices: germanium electron mobility 0.39 m2/Vs and hole mobility 0.19 m2/Vs at 300 K
